name: bitblocks-election-count-vectors
description: Test vectors for the counting rule of an open-ballot election recorded on BSV: who may vote, which ballots count, the tally and the winners. Each vector gives the input and the outcome to match, so anyone can recount an election archive with their own code and check it against ours.
claim: These vectors cover the count only. They take as given that each ballot's signer is the key whose AIP signature checked, and that each height is on the chain the headers agree on. Checking signatures, tx bytes, merkle proofs and headers comes before the count.
draft_fields: The record field names (election, seats, candidates, opens_at_height, closes_at_height, members, choices) are a draft until the first election record is published. The rule and the outcomes here won't change within v1.
versioning: Within v1, a vector's id, input and expected outcome stay as they are, except to correct a mistake, which the version number and this file will show. New vectors raise the minor version. A change to the rule gets a new file.
how_to_use: For each vector, run your counter on input.election, input.roll and input.ballots, with input.close_block_hash when it is present.
Compare your answer with expected. Ballots are listed in chain order: by height, then position, with unconfirmed ballots last by txid.
Where expected has error, a counter refuses the whole input. error_detail is the wording Bitblocks uses, so yours may differ.
Signers, txids and candidate ids are opaque strings compared exactly. In real records a signer is an address and a txid is 64 hex characters.

fields.election: The election record: election (its id), seats, candidates (each id and name), and the window opens_at_height to closes_at_height, both ends included.
fields.roll: members: the keys allowed to vote.
fields.ballot: txid; election (the id it names); height (null while unconfirmed or after a reorg removed its block); position (its index in the block, so two ballots in one block have an order); signer (the key whose AIP signature checked, or null); choices (candidate ids).
fields.close_block_hash: The hash of the block at closes_at_height, lowercase hex as explorers show it. Known only after close, it settles a tie for the last seats.
fields.expected.ballots: Each ballot's txid, counted, rule (the first rule it failed, or null) and replaced_by (the txid that replaced it, or null).
fields.expected.tally: Votes per candidate, in the election's order, zeros included. A ballot gives one vote to each candidate it names.
fields.expected.winners: Candidates with at least one vote, most votes first, up to seats. Candidates tied above the boundary all win, in the election's order. A tie for the last seats goes by lot (see tie_rule), listed in lot order.
fields.expected.undecided: null, or the seats still open and the tied candidates for them, when a tie for the last seats has no close_block_hash to settle it.

rules.no_signature: 2. No AIP signature checked (signer is null).
rules.unconfirmed: 4. It isn't in a block (height is null).
rules.malformed_choices: 6. choices isn't a list of strings.
rules.too_many_choices: 7. It names more than seats candidates.
rules.unknown_candidate: 9. It names an id not in candidates.
rules.replaced: 10. The same signer has a later ballot, in chain order, that passed rules 1 to 9; replaced_by is its txid.

rule_order: A ballot is listed against the first rule it fails, in the order numbered in rules. Only a ballot that passes rules 1 to 9 can replace another.
tie_rule: When candidates tie for the last seats, order them by sha256 of the UTF-8 string "<close_block_hash>:<candidate id>", as lowercase hex, lowest first, and fill the seats left. The block at closes_at_height isn't known while voting is open, so no one can steer the lot, and anyone can check it from the headers.

vectors.description: Four members vote inside the window. Every ballot counts; Ada and Ben take the two seats.
The window includes both ends: a ballot at opens_at_height and one at closes_at_height count, one a block before or after doesn't.
A ballot signed by a key that isn't on the roll is listed and not counted.
A ballot whose AIP signature didn't check has signer null and doesn't count.
A ballot for another election is listed against the rule it fails first, and not counted.
A ballot not yet in a block (height null), or whose block a reorg removed, waits: it doesn't count until it confirms.
With two seats: three names is too many, one name twice is a duplicate, and an id not on the list is unknown. None of them counts.
A member votes twice. The later one in chain order counts, and the earlier one is replaced by it.
Two ballots from one member in the same block: the higher position is later and counts. Input order doesn't matter; the ballots are given here in reverse.
A later ballot that fails a rule (here an unknown candidate, and one after close) doesn't replace the member's earlier counted ballot.
An empty ballot is valid and votes for no one, so a later empty ballot withdraws the member's earlier votes.
Ada and Ben tie for first with two seats to fill. Both win, listed in the election's order; no lot is needed.
Ada leads; Ben, Cy and Di tie for the last seat. Without close_block_hash (voting still open) that seat is undecided.

The same ballots, with the hash of the block at closes_at_height. Each tied candidate's lot is sha256 of "<close_block_hash>:<id>" as lowercase hex: ben cdb52145fbc5619e76482acef5bdcd3306932587ba8b9a287b5b7a62417a1ebe, cy 2f609dcdfe47fafe4383bfbb445a5e0075adafa2d44ec953a402c0d1455141a6, di ca5e18ad2c5c8d844210c10363f960bae6a19f5a718eb7fab7d47dfcec6cdfa3. The lowest, cy, takes the seat.
A candidate needs at least one vote to win, so with three seats and two candidates voted for, one seat stays empty.
A ballot that fails several rules is listed against the first, in the order in rules: here an outsider's late ballot with too many names is not_on_roll.
The same txid twice is a broken input, not a ballot to judge. A counter refuses the whole input.
Two different txids at the same height and position can't both be in the chain.

expected.error_detail: another ballot has this height and position

vectors.description: An election that closes before it opens can't be counted.
